regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 56.5","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% YoY is the headline; the quality check is IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity — both confirm the expansion is investment-led, not a statistical artefact. PMI Composite at 56.5 corroborates, with manufacturing (55.7) and services (55.8) moving in lockstep. The inversion: core sector at 4.8% YoY, down from 5.0%, is the one proxy that refuses to confirm the acceleration — cement and steel dispatch are the real capex barometer, and they are softening at the margin.","badge_label":"Expansion Mode","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 6.09% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"CPI at 6.09% YoY is 99 bps above the RBI's upper tolerance band, but the decomposition matters: core CPI at 4.5% YoY is contained, while fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY — a 95th-percentile print — is doing the damage. The second-order effect is underappreciated: fuel feeds into WPI at 9.92% YoY, which feeds into manufacturing input costs with a two-quarter lag, threatening core CPI just as the RBI is being pressured to cut. The RBI's own forecast of 5.1% YoY is already stale — Brent at $92.24/bbl has not corrected.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 19.54% YoY; CD ratio 82%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 19.54% YoY against deposit growth at 16.86% YoY — a 268 bps divergence widening for three consecutive months — has pushed the CD ratio to 82%, a 10-year-high percentile. Services credit at 28.3% YoY (rising four months in a row) is the accelerant; NBFC credit growth at 15.4% YoY, slipping from 15.8%, signals wholesale funding is already repricing. The historical precedent is instructive: the last time the CD ratio sustained above 80% during a rate pause, the regulator responded with risk-weight tightening on unsecured lending within two quarters. The incentive to act is there; the question is timing.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. is unchanged, but the real rate is being compressed by the inflation overshoot — at 6.09% CPI, the ex-ante real rate is negative. The RBI's pause is defensible only if fuel inflation is transitory; with Brent holding above $90/bbl and the FAO food index at 136 (up from 134.5), that assumption is weakening. For housing, the average home loan rate at 7.35% p.a. is already above the affordability threshold for mid-segment buyers — a rate cut would help, but the RBI cannot cut into a 6.09% CPI print without losing credibility on its 4% target.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.9% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY (up from 16.1%) and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (up from 75.6%) together confirm the private capex upcycle is not a budget line item — it is showing up in actual output. The 77.4% utilisation print matters because 75% is the empirical threshold above which Indian corporates historically commit to greenfield investment; we are now 240 bps above it. Iron ore at $161.91/t — up sharply from $90.64/t — is the commodity signal that construction and steel demand are real. The risk: core sector at 4.8% YoY is the lagging confirmation that hasn't arrived yet.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹231290 cr/mo; PV 32.1% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹2,31,290 cr / month (90th percentile) is the broadest consumption signal available — but the question is whether this is demand or formalisation. Passenger vehicle sales at 32.1% YoY and two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY suggest the answer is both: urban discretionary is strong, and rural mobility (two-wheelers) is recovering after three weak months. The divergence to watch: e-commerce GMV growth at 25% YoY (up from 18%) confirms urban digital consumption, while the absence of affordable housing sales data leaves the rural/semi-urban demand picture incomplete. GST is the floor; it is not the ceiling.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 19.54% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 16.86% YoY — a 268 bps divergence widening for 3 consecutive months (17.1%→19.4%→19.54% credit; 17.8%→16.86% deposits). CD ratio now 82% credit-to-deposits, up from 81% last month. Services credit surging 28.3% YoY (21.4%→22.9%→24.3%→28.3% over 4 months) while agriculture credit at 19.5% YoY. NBFC credit growth at 15.4% YoY, down from 15.8%, signals wholesale funding stress.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios >45% — they'll poach deposits from smaller lenders. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding >30% of liabilities; they face margin compression and refinancing risk. RBI will likely signal deposit-friendly measures (higher savings rates, CRR cuts) within 2-3 months. Corporate bond issuance at ₹134,000 cr/month shows firms are already bypassing banks.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile historically; last time it breached 82% was 2022 when RBI tightened. Deposit growth at 82nd percentile suggests retail is pulling back — watch for CASA deterioration.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Upcycle Accelerating Into Q4","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY (prev 16.1%), capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (prev 75.6%), both rising. Capacity utilisation now at 68th percentile — above the 75% threshold that historically triggers fresh capex. Core sector growth at 4.8% YoY (down from 5% but still positive). Iron ore prices up sharply to $161.91/t from $90.64/t, signalling construction & steel demand. Nifty 50 at 25,839 (87th percentile), Bank Nifty at 63,326 (100th percentile) — equity markets pricing in capex cycle.","implication":"Overweight capital goods, cement, and steel stocks. Increase exposure to project-linked companies (EPC, infrastructure). Private capex will likely accelerate in Q4 FY26 as capacity utilisation stays elevated. Avoid defensive sectors; rotation into cyclicals justified. Monitor order books in auto, infra, and power — they should show 12-18 month visibility.","pct_10y":68,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 68th percentile is mid-cycle; historically, 77%+ has preceded 18-month capex booms. IIP capital goods at 53rd percentile suggests this is early-stage, not late-cycle.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP Inflows Hit 94th Percentile, But Growth Slowing","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,160 cr/month (94th percentile), down marginally from ₹32,490 cr/month. SIP YoY growth at 8.9% (28th percentile) — a sharp deceleration from 15% → 19.85% → 14% → 10.7% over prior 4 months. MF AUM at ₹83.39 lakh cr (86th percentile), up from ₹82.64 lakh cr. Equity MF net inflows at ₹32,994 cr/month (78th percentile). However, SIP accounts at 10 mn (3rd percentile) — data anomaly suggests reporting issue, but trend shows retail participation is broad.","implication":"SIP flows remain structural support for equity markets, but growth deceleration is a yellow flag. Affluent retail (higher ticket sizes) is entering late-cycle; average SIP size likely rising even as account growth slows. Maintain overweight on large-cap, dividend-paying stocks that appeal to SIP investors. Watch for SIP growth to stabilise at 8-10% YoY — if it drops below 5%, retail fatigue is setting in.","pct_10y":94,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 94th percentile are near all-time highs, but YoY growth at 28th percentile signals deceleration. This divergence (high absolute flows, low growth rate) is typical of late-expansion retail participation.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation at 95th Percentile, Import Bill Rising","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile), up from 20.05% YoY — a 288 bps jump. Brent crude at $92.24/bbl (68th percentile), WTI at $85.73/bbl (67th percentile), both rising. Natural gas at $3.599/MMBtu (51st percentile). FAO food index at 136 (63rd percentile), up from 134.5. CPI headline at 6.09% YoY (57th percentile), core CPI at 4.5% YoY (42nd percentile) — fuel is the primary driver of headline inflation overshoot. RBI inflation forecast at 5.1% YoY (54th percentile), up from 4.6%.","implication":"India's current account deficit will widen if oil stays >$90/bbl. Hedge INR weakness — fuel inflation will keep RBI on pause despite growth strength. Avoid refiners with weak hedges; prefer integrated oil majors. Reduce exposure to discretionary consumption (auto, durables) as fuel costs compress margins. Monitor CAD closely; if oil averages $95+ in Q4, expect INR pressure to 93-94 levels.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile is extreme; last time it was this high was 2022 during the Russia-Ukraine shock. This is a structural headwind to RBI's rate-cut cycle.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"risk","title":"Fed Tightening, BOJ Hiking, Carry Unwind Risk","data_text":"Fed funds rate at 3.88% p.a. (75th percentile), up from 3.75% p.a., rising 3 in a row (3.63%→3.63%→3.75%→3.88%). US 10Y Treasury at 4.91% yield (89th percentile), falling 5 in a row (5.12%→5.1%→5.07%→5.04%→4.92%→4.91%) — inversion flattening. BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. US CPI at 3.72% YoY (56th percentile), core PCE at 3.26% YoY (61st percentile).","implication":"Carry trades are unwinding — JPY strength will pressure INR and EM currencies. Prefer India's domestic-demand stories over export-linked plays.","pct_10y":89,"pct_note":"US 10Y at 89th percentile and BOJ at 100th percentile represent a rare policy divergence. Last time BOJ hiked while Fed was still high was 2006 — it preceded a carry unwind and EM stress.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"watch","title":"INR Stable But Vulnerable to Oil Shocks","data_text":"INR at 92.59 ₹/USD (85th percentile), flat from 92.6 ₹/USD. signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Collapse Signals GCC Pullback","data_text":"Office absorption at 4.02 mn sq ft/quarter (0th percentile, strong-negative signal: -100), down from 19.5 mn sq ft/quarter last period. Office vacancy at 13.4% (37th percentile), down from 14.5%, but absorption data shows a cliff. Nifty IT at flat performance despite office absorption collapse. Airline passenger traffic at 8.64 mn/month (0th percentile, strong-negative signal: -100), a data anomaly (35.08 → 86.4 → 8.64), but suggests travel weakness. Retail mall vacancy at 11.15% (37th percentile), oscillating. Meanwhile, GST collections at ₹231,290 cr/month (90th percentile) and PV sales at 32.1% YoY (60th percentile) remain strong — consumption is NOT collapsing.","implication":"Global Capability Centres (GCCs) are pulling back on office leasing, not traditional IT services. This decouples commercial RE from IT stock performance — Nifty IT can stay flat while office REITs (Embassy, Mindspace, Brookfield) face headwinds. The office market is bifurcating: tier-1 (Mumbai, Bangalore) seeing GCC consolidation, tier-2 facing vacancy. Underweight commercial RE REITs; overweight residential (affordability index at 2.3x, 5th percentile, is a strong buy signal). Watch for GCC announcements in Q4 — if they signal further consolidation, office REITs will re-rate lower.","pct_10y":0,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 0th percentile is a structural shift, not cyclical. GCCs are optimising real estate post-pandemic; this is a multi-year headwind for commercial RE. Residential, by contrast, is at affordability extremes (2.3x price-to-income, 5th percentile) — a rare entry point.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

Strong Headline, Softening Core — Fuel Doing the Inflation's Heavy Lifting

The facts:

  • GDP at 7.8% YoY with PMI Composite at 56.5 and IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY confirm broad expansion.
  • GST collections at ₹2,31,290 cr / month (90th percentile) and PV sales at 32.1% YoY signal demand is not narrowing.
  • But CPI at 6.09% YoY — 99 bps above the RBI's upper band — is driven by fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile), not by core demand.
  • Core CPI at 4.5% YoY (42nd percentile) is contained; the inflation problem is imported, not structural — for now.

The tension: Growth is investment-led and consumption is broad-based, yet the inflation overshoot is entirely fuel-driven — a supply shock the RBI cannot cure with rate hikes, but cannot ignore without losing its anchor.

Bottom line: Watch core CPI: if it crosses 5.0% YoY as WPI input costs transmit, the RBI's pause becomes untenable regardless of the growth picture.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

US Re-Accelerates, BOJ Tightens — EM Carry Trade Has a Countdown Clock

The facts:

  • US GDP SAAR at 4.3% SAAR (rising four quarters in a row) with PMI Composite at 58.4 (80th percentile) — the US is not slowing.
  • But US 10Y Treasury at 4.91% yield has fallen five sessions in a row from 5.12% — bond markets are pricing a growth peak the data does not yet support.
  • BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile, rising two in a row) is unwinding the yen carry trade that funded EM inflows for a decade.
  • China PMI Composite at 49.5 (contraction) with CPI at 0.7% YoY removes the commodity reflation backstop for India's export sector.

The tension: DM equity markets (S&P 500 at 100th percentile, Euro Stoxx at 100th percentile) are pricing re-acceleration; bond markets and China data are pricing deceleration. One of them is wrong, and India's FII flows will feel the correction.

Bottom line: BOJ at 1.25% p.a. is the underpriced tail risk — the next 25 bps hike triggers yen carry unwind and EM outflows within 60 days.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

SIP Plateau Meets DII Retreat — Domestic Absorption Is Thinning

The facts:

  • SIP inflows at ₹32,160 cr / month (94th percentile) remain elevated in level, but YoY growth at 8.9% YoY (28th percentile) has decelerated from 19.85% four months ago.
  • DII equity net at ₹6,222 cr net / month — down sharply from ₹51,829 cr net / month last period — means the domestic absorption buffer has thinned by 88%.
  • FII equity net at −₹4,516 cr net / month remains negative, with a five-month range of −₹49,935 cr to +₹29,631 cr — structurally volatile.
  • But MF AUM at ₹83.39 lakh cr (86th percentile) and corp bond issuance at ₹1,34,000 cr / month (52nd percentile) confirm the system is not illiquid.

The tension: SIP inflows are high in absolute terms but decelerating in growth — the retail bid that cushioned FII exits in prior months is losing momentum precisely as DII net buying collapses.

Bottom line: If SIP YoY growth falls below 7% next month, the domestic absorption backstop for any FII sell-off becomes structurally insufficient.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

REITs Pricing Office Collapse; Residential Splits Between Hyderabad and Chennai

The facts:

  • NRI buying is FALLING — NRI share of residential purchases at 18% (down 2 pp), with NRI share within premium/luxury at 32%; remittances at $155.1 bn (14.5% YoY) have not translated into sustained purchase momentum.
  • Hyderabad leads residential with sales +15% YoY and launches +120% YoY; Chennai is the other end at sales −10% YoY — a 25 pp spread within the same macro cycle.
  • Office absorption at 4.02 mn sq ft / quarter (0th percentile, down from 19.5 mn sq ft / quarter) has collapsed; Embassy REIT at ₹370, Mindspace at ₹345, Brookfield at ₹263 — all down 10–28% from prior prints.
  • But Bank Nifty at 63,326 (100th percentile) and Nifty 50 at 25,839 (87th percentile) price a credit and growth cycle that the office absorption data directly contradicts.

The tension: Equity markets are pricing a GCC-led services expansion; office absorption data shows GCCs pulled back sharply this quarter. REIT prices have adjusted; Nifty IT has not.

Bottom line: Avoid office REITs until absorption recovers above 12 mn sq ft / quarter; within residential, overweight Hyderabad and Bengaluru, underweight Chennai and Pune.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Three Fuses, One Detonator — Fuel, Carry, and Credit

The facts:

  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) with Brent at $92.24/bbl — every $10 rise adds ~$15 bn to India's annual import bill and widens CAD by ~40 bps; INR at 92.59 has no buffer if oil breaks $100.
  • BOJ at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile) — the next hike triggers yen carry unwind; FII equity net has already swung −₹49,935 cr in a single month this cycle.
  • CD ratio at 82% (75th percentile) with services credit at 28.3% YoY — macro-prudential tightening via risk weights on unsecured lending is the regulatory response history suggests; NBFC funding costs rise first.
  • Office absorption at 4.02 mn sq ft / quarter (0th percentile) — if GCC leasing does not recover in Q4, Nifty IT earnings estimates carry 8–12% downside.

The tension: All three primary risks — oil, carry unwind, credit tightening — are externally triggered but domestically amplified; India's $680 bn FX reserve buffer buys time, not immunity.

Bottom line: Watch Brent this week: a close above $95/bbl forces the RBI's hand on FX intervention and makes the inflation pause narrative untenable.

"}
